lead: The DA has opened coalition talks with Zuma's MK Party as KwaZulu-Natal's hung councils look for majorities, while the ANC's NEC kept Ramaphosa in place and leaned towards deal-by-deal coalitions. Tonight the Springboks face France in Paris and Bafana host Kenya.

items.title: DA reaches out to MK Party for coalition talks in KZN
items.summary: DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis wrote to Jacob Zuma proposing talks, and MK has accepted, with a meeting expected within days. Both sides cautioned that ideological gaps make a deal far from certain, especially in eThekwini and Msunduzi.

items.title: ANC NEC backs Ramaphosa, weighs metro-by-metro coalition deals
items.summary: No NEC member called for the president to step down at Thursday's Boksburg meeting, sources said. The party is leaning towards case-by-case municipal deals and is unlikely to accept the DA's bid to lead most metros; councils must sit by 26 November.

items.title: eThekwini: DA's Hoosen confident of mayoralty as MK holds 86 seats
items.summary: MK has 86 of 223 seats, the DA 57, the ANC 37 and the IFP 15, with 112 needed to govern. DA mayoral candidate Haniff Hoosen says talks are under way but nothing is final.

items.title: MK Party drops claims that the IEC rigged the 2024 election
items.summary: After a Durban High Court dispute over remarks made in Umlazi, MK and the IEC agreed to withdraw the case. MK says it respects court rulings clearing the commission; it won about 34% in KZN this month, where 34 councils are hung.

items.title: MK, EFF and SACP form left bloc, set terms for backing the ANC
items.summary: The new Council of the Left, which also includes ACT and others, says it holds about a fifth of the municipal vote. It wants the ANC to adopt its programme and cut ties with the DA and FF Plus before it offers support.

items.title: Intelligence chief tells Madlanga commission crime networks are inside the state
items.summary: Acting Nicoc coordinator Ntandazo Sifolo said assessments since 2022 flagged a merger of political and criminal interests. He also said Ramaphosa got a verbal intelligence briefing on 30 June 2025, days before Mkhwanazi went public.

items.title: New coalition guidelines aim to curb abuse of no-confidence motions
items.summary: Cogta Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa has asked councils to set their own rules for such motions and has issued a template coalition agreement, to make hung municipalities more stable ahead of their first sittings.

items.title: Gauteng warns of malaria spike linked to regional travel
items.summary: The province recorded 768 cases and 17 deaths from January to September, most linked to travel in SADC countries, chiefly Mozambique. Officials urge travellers to visit a clinic first and report fever promptly.

items.title: Houthis claim new strikes on Saudi oil sites; UN extends Yemen sanctions
items.summary: Saudi forces said they downed drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province, while the Houthis claimed hits on pipeline and Yanbu facilities. The Security Council unanimously renewed sanctions on Yemen for a year.

items.title: Trump says Gulf allies asked him to hold off on further Iran strikes
items.summary: Speaking at the White House, the US president said Gulf states had requested a pause in additional attacks on Iran.

items.title: Israeli strike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital kills six
items.summary: Gaza health officials said a doctor was among those killed in Khan Younis. Israel said it targeted a senior Hamas member; the UN warned the attack threatens the fragile ceasefire.

items.title: European leaders meet in Dublin as hybrid attacks hit schools
items.summary: More than 40 countries met at the European Political Community summit amid hoax bomb threats to thousands of Italian schools. Europe is also seeking an envoy for US-backed Ukraine peace talks.

items.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases
items.summary: Official data show 11,042 cases and at least 5,387 deaths in eight provinces, making it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. The Bundibugyo strain has no specific vaccine yet; trials are under way.

items.title: Amnesty says UN and South Sudan ignored warnings before village attack
items.summary: The rights group says peacekeepers and officials were warned before a March attack on Abiemnom that killed over 200 people. It wants an independent probe ahead of South Sudan's 22 December elections.

items.title: Rand weaker near R16.75 as US rate-hike bets build
items.summary: The rand has slipped from about R16.53 midweek after hot US inflation data lifted expectations of a Federal Reserve hike in December. Gold was near $3,974 an ounce and oil around $91 a barrel.

items.title: Thursday market snapshot: rand at R16.61, Woolworths slump weighs
items.summary: BusinessTech put the rand at R16.61 to the dollar on Thursday, with traders fully pricing a December Fed hike. Woolworths closed 8.5% lower, its worst day since March 2020.

items.title: SARB rate decision due next Thursday, 19 November
items.summary: The repo rate is 7.25% and prime 10.75% after September's 25-basis-point hike. The Monetary Policy Committee announces its next decision around 3pm on 19 November.

items.title: Springboks take on France in Paris tonight
items.summary: Siya Kolisi leads the Boks for the 70th time at Stade de France, kick-off 10:10pm SA time. Wilco Louw starts at tighthead and Eben Etzebeth is left out.

items.title: Bafana host Benni McCarthy's Kenya in AFCON qualifier at 6pm
items.summary: Group D leaders South Africa play in Johannesburg tonight, with the return leg in Nairobi on Tuesday. Kenya arrive amid unpaid allowances, and McCarthy says his staff have not been paid for three months.

items.title: Tatjana Smith switches to swim for the Netherlands
items.summary: South Africa's most decorated Olympian, who holds Dutch citizenship, cited financial and practical challenges. She is targeting LA 2028 and plans to keep training in South Africa.

items.title: Sundowns Ladies reach CAF Women's Champions League final
items.summary: They beat Kawempe Muslim Ladies 4-1 in the semi-final and meet defending champions AS FAR of Morocco on Sunday. The Proteas also open their Test series against Bangladesh in Johannesburg on Sunday.

items.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress takes over for now
items.summary: Huang left the chipmaker and its board after 33 years following reports of affairs and alleged links to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The board is searching for a permanent successor.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly targets Nasdaq debut next week
items.summary: The AI company is reported to be seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, with trading under the ticker ANT expected around 19 or 20 November.
